response.summary: Both round-2 findings are fixed in the current source and in the captures. The teacher link now reads "Teacher home" (app.js:34). In teacher-768-text2.png it wraps to "Teacher / home" inside the active pill without clipping. Assignment rows use flex-wrap with .assignment-body{flex:1 1 10rem} at every width, and the h3 uses overflow-wrap:normal (style.css:5). In text-200-home-1048.png, "Conditional Indicators Refresher" breaks only between words and Open moves to its own line. Because --sidebar-width is clamp(205px,14rem,260px) (style.css:3), the main offsets at style.css:5/11 stay matched. In both enlarged captures the Messages "1" badge and the nav labels stay inside the sidebar. At the user's 1048x858 viewport (home-1048-viewport.png), the type is clearly better than in 09: ordinary-case labels, a single "Ctrl K" badge, Newsreader only on the greeting heading, readable muted secondary text, quick actions with whole labels, and the coach and session panels intact. home-768.png stacks cleanly and nothing clips. The keyboard shortcut handler still matches only the platform's modifier and is ignored while a dialog is open (app.js:109). The inherited behaviour I traced in source is unchanged: exact reference parsing, fixed Review totals, work filters, draft/note save-failure retention, dialog focus return and route guards. I found no material regression. One low-severity cosmetic issue remains: avatars have a fixed pixel size, so their initials overflow the circle at 200% text.

findings.evidence: The avatar circle is sized in px but its initials are sized in rem. At 200% text the coach avatar is .8125rem×2 = 26px Manrope semibold "JF", which is about as wide as or wider than its 29px circle. In text-200-home-1048.png the coach-panel "JF" shows no visible circle around it and sits above the line of "Joshua". The sidebar-foot "JF" in teacher-768-text2.png likewise fills its 32px circle edge to edge. Round 1 fixed chips and dots by moving them to rem/em, but the avatars were not changed. The host's chipOverflow check apparently doesn't include .avatar. This is cosmetic, and no information is lost.
findings.fix: Size avatars in em relative to their own font, e.g. .avatar{width:2.3em;height:2.3em} and .message .avatar{width:2.2em;height:2.2em}, or use min-width/min-height in rem. Add .avatar to the chip-bounds check.

coverage: Source read in full: index.html, app.js (117 lines), style.css (17 lines). I compared the source against reviews/round-3-source-hashes.json (index 6706D017…, app 3061FF96…, style EC3F267D…) but did not compute any hashes myself.
